name: reCAPTCHA v3 Enterprise on every page
plain: Google reCAPTCHA v3 Enterprise scores each page load without any visible challenge.
meaning: Sends page behavior and device signals to Google to get a bot risk score. Invisible to the person; Google sets its own cookies and receives IP and browser data.

steps: Token sent with tracking payload for server verification

limits.headline: Can score every page visit for bot behavior without showing a challenge
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens each time a LinkedIn page loads
can: Watch how the page is used to judge if you are a bot
Send a score about the visit to LinkedIn
Share device and browser signals with Google for the score
cannot: Show a puzzle or ask you to click anything in v3
See other tabs, files or apps
Work if blocked, though blocking may stop the page from loading

story.what_it_is: An invisible Google check that scores every page load for bot risk.

marketing.name: reCAPTCHA Enterprise
marketing.pitch: Google pitches it as a way to detect bots and fraud with a risk score and no puzzle for real people.

story.for_you: You never see a puzzle or a box. The page quietly sends signals about your browser and clicks to Google, which sends back a score. If the score is bad, the site may then ask you to prove you are real.
story.for_makers: Fake logins, scraping and spam are constant. A score without a puzzle keeps real people moving fast while bots get stopped. The price is that Google gets a signal of your visit to the site, plus your IP and browser data.

use_cases.example: A login page on LinkedIn gets a score for each visit, and asks for extra proof only when the score looks bot like.
A ticket site uses the score to push likely bots to the back of the queue.
A checkout page asks reCAPTCHA about a card test, and blocks it when it looks like a bot testing stolen cards.
A game sign up page scores each new account to stop bot farms that sell gold or cheat.
A comment form scores each post to stop spam bots before they add links.
A team removes bot traffic from its reports using the same score.

risks: Real people may be wrongly flagged

technical_bounds: Google decides what signals it reads
Frequency (every page) is reported by BrowserGate, 35 reCAPTCHA references in the snapshot

legit_uses: Cheap bot filtering with no friction
abuse: Third party sees every page view
